tables.name: product_signups
tables.purpose: Records each customer's request to be notified when a specific product variant returns to stock, and tracks whether the notification was delivered.

columns.name: variant_external_id
columns.purpose: numeric Shopify variant ID the customer is waiting on

columns.name: product_external_id
columns.purpose: numeric Shopify product ID for admin filtering and display

columns.name: failure_reason
columns.purpose: populated when status='failed' so admin dashboard surfaces reason inline

columns.name: resolved_at
columns.purpose: set when status transitions to notified, failed, or unsubscribed

tables.name: notification_attempts
tables.purpose: Logs every email delivery attempt for a signup so the merchant can audit successes and failures and the system can prove a notification was sent exactly once.

columns.name: signup_id
columns.constraints: NOT NULL REFERENCES product_signups(id) ON DELETE CASCADE
columns.purpose: links this attempt to the originating signup record

columns.name: variant_external_id
columns.purpose: denormalised for querying attempts by variant without joining

transitions.trigger: restock webhook fires and email is delivered successfully
email delivery attempt returns a permanent or terminal-transient failure
customer explicitly cancels signup via widget or admin
variant details fetch fails (variant deleted or unavailable)

widget.purpose: Return whether the current customer is already signed up for back-in-stock notification for a given product variant.
Register a customer's email address to receive a one-time notification when a specific product variant is back in stock.
Unsubscribe a customer from a back-in-stock notification for a specific product variant.

admin.purpose: Return a paginated, filterable list of all back-in-stock signups and their notification outcomes for the merchant dashboard.

responseShape.items: { id: string, variant_external_id: string, product_external_id: string, customer_email: string, status: string, failure_reason: string|null, created_at: string, resolved_at: string|null }[]

widget-get-signup-state.description: Return whether a customer already holds an active signup for a given product variant so the widget renders the correct initial state.

steps.purpose: reject request if either required query param is missing
look up existing signup for this customer-variant pair
steps.template: SELECT id, status FROM product_signups WHERE customer_email = ${customerEmail} AND variant_external_id = ${variantExternalId} LIMIT 1

steps.purpose: determine signup state from query result
steps.expression: existing.length > 0 ? { is_signed_up: existing[0].status === 'pending', status: existing[0].status } : { is_signed_up: false, status: null }

steps.purpose: return signup state to widget

postconditions: response always contains is_signed_up boolean and status string or null
edgeCases: Customer has no signup for this variant — is_signed_up=false, status=null.
Customer has a notified or unsubscribed signup — is_signed_up=false with the actual terminal status returned so the widget can show appropriate messaging.

widget-register-signup.description: Create a pending signup record linking a customer email to a product variant, enforcing one active signup per customer-variant pair.

steps.purpose: reject request if required fields are missing

body.error: variant_external_id, product_external_id, and customer_email are required

steps.purpose: sanitize email to remove null bytes
insert signup or do nothing if a row already exists for this customer-variant pair, returning the row
steps.template: INSERT INTO product_signups (variant_external_id, product_external_id, customer_email, status) VALUES (${variantExternalId}, ${productExternalId}, ${cleanEmail}, 'pending') ON CONFLICT (customer_email, variant_external_id) DO NOTHING RETURNING id, status

steps.purpose: record signup registration outcome for observability
return success regardless of whether row was newly inserted or was a duplicate

postconditions: at most one pending signup row exists per customer_email + variant_external_id pair
duplicate submissions return success without creating a second row
edgeCases: Customer submits form twice for same variant — ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING returns zero rows; response is still success=true.

Customer previously unsubscribed for this variant — the existing terminal row is left untouched; a new pending signup cannot be created until the old row is removed; the widget should reflect the existing status.

widget-cancel-signup.description: Mark a customer's pending signup as unsubscribed so no future notification is sent for that variant.

steps.purpose: reject request if required fields are missing
claim the unsubscribe transition atomically using workflow helper
steps.expression: await workflow.claim('product_signups', null, { from: 'pending', to: 'unsubscribed', extraWhere: sql`AND customer_email = ${customerEmail} AND variant_external_id = ${variantExternalId}`, statusColumn: 'status' })

steps.purpose: skip if no pending signup was found for this customer-variant pair

ifTrue.purpose: record that no pending signup was found to cancel
ifTrue.message: unsubscribe: no pending signup found, treating as no-op

steps.purpose: stamp resolved_at on the now-unsubscribed signup
steps.template: UPDATE product_signups SET resolved_at = now() WHERE id = ${signupId}

steps.purpose: record successful unsubscribe
return success to widget

postconditions: signup row status is 'unsubscribed' with resolved_at set after successful call
idempotent: calling remove when no pending signup exists returns success
edgeCases: Customer unsubscribes after the signup was already notified or failed — claim returns null because status != pending; treated as a no-op success.
Concurrent unsubscribe calls for the same signup — workflow.claim is atomic; exactly one succeeds and the other gets null.

admin-list-signups.description: Return a paginated, status-filtered list of all back-in-stock signups and their notification outcomes for the merchant dashboard.

steps.purpose: fetch signups filtered by status when provided, ordered by created_at desc
steps.template: SELECT id, variant_external_id, product_external_id, customer_email, status, failure_reason, created_at, resolved_at FROM product_signups WHERE (${statusFilter}::text IS NULL OR status = ${statusFilter}) ORDER BY created_at DESC

steps.purpose: return paginated signup list

postconditions: response always contains items array, total count, page, and page_size
when status_filter is null all signups across all statuses are returned
edgeCases: status_filter value not in the enum set — no rows match; returns empty items array with total=0.
page exceeds total pages — paginate helper returns empty items array.

handle-inventory-update.description: When inventory for a variant rises above zero, fetch pending signups for that variant, retrieve variant details from Shopify, and send a one-time restock notification email to each pending customer, recording the outcome and advancing each signup to its terminal state.

steps.purpose: null-defend variant id and inventory quantity from webhook payload (R3)
steps.expression: { variantId: variantIdRaw ?? null, qty: inventoryQuantity ?? null }

steps.purpose: exit if variant id is missing or inventory is not above zero

ifTrue.purpose: record skip reason for ops visibility
ifTrue.message: inventory_levels/update: skipping — variant missing or qty not positive

ifTrue.purpose: exit early — not a positive-stock restock event

steps.purpose: fetch all pending signups for this variant to determine whether any notifications need to be sent
steps.template: SELECT id, customer_email, status FROM product_signups WHERE variant_external_id = ${variantId} AND status = 'pending'

steps.purpose: exit early when no pending signups exist for this variant

ifTrue.purpose: record no-op for duplicate or already-processed restock event

steps.purpose: build Shopify GID for the product variant (R10)
fetch variant details from Shopify; on failure mark all pending signups as failed with reason 'variant unavailable'

try.purpose: retrieve variant title, availableForSale, and parent product title and handle for the notification email
try.query: query GetRestockedVariant($id: ID!) { productVariant(id: $id) { id title availableForSale product { id title handle } } }

try.purpose: treat event as no-op if variant is not available for sale

ifTrue.message: inventory_levels/update: variant not availableForSale — skipping notifications

ifTrue.purpose: exit — variant not purchasable, preserve signups for genuine restock

catch.purpose: mark every pending signup as failed because variant details could not be fetched

steps.purpose: advance signup to failed with variant-unavailable reason
steps.template: UPDATE product_signups SET status = 'failed', failure_reason = ${reason}, resolved_at = now() WHERE id = ${signupId} AND status = 'pending'

steps.purpose: log notification attempt as failed_permanent for variant-unavailable signups
steps.template: INSERT INTO notification_attempts (signup_id, variant_external_id, outcome, failure_reason) VALUES (${signupId}, ${variantId}, 'failed_permanent', ${reason})

catch.purpose: record variant fetch failure for ops alerting
catch.message: inventory_levels/update: variant fetch failed — all signups marked failed

catch.purpose: exit after marking all signups failed

steps.purpose: build the storefront product URL from the product handle
for each pending signup, atomically claim it then send the notification email and record the outcome
atomically transition this signup from pending to notified, ensuring only one concurrent restock wave sends an email (R1)
steps.template: UPDATE product_signups SET status = 'notified', resolved_at = now() WHERE id = ${signupId} AND status = 'pending' RETURNING id, customer_email

steps.purpose: send notification email and record attempt; on failure revert signup to failed with reason

try.purpose: deliver the back-in-stock notification to the customer

try.template: INSERT INTO notification_attempts (signup_id, variant_external_id, outcome) VALUES (${signupId}, ${variantId}, 'sent')

catch.purpose: revert signup to failed state and record the email delivery failure reason (R4)
catch.template: UPDATE product_signups SET status = 'failed', failure_reason = ${reason}, resolved_at = now() WHERE id = ${signupId}

catch.purpose: log failed notification attempt with failure reason
catch.template: INSERT INTO notification_attempts (signup_id, variant_external_id, outcome, failure_reason) VALUES (${signupId}, ${variantId}, 'failed_permanent', ${reason})

steps.purpose: summarise restock notification run outcome

postconditions: every signup that was pending at handler start is now in status notified, failed, or unsubscribed — never left in pending after a completed run
every notification attempt (success or failure) has a corresponding row in notification_attempts
no signup is emailed more than once: the sql_claim atomic update from pending prevents duplicate sends
edgeCases: Duplicate webhook delivery after all signups already notified — pendingSignups.length === 0 short-circuits before any Shopify or email call.
Customer unsubscribes between webhook receipt and the for_each iteration reaching their row — sql_claim finds status != pending, returns zero rows, zeroRowAction=skip skips email send.
Concurrent second webhook delivery while first is mid-loop — sql_claim is atomic; the second delivery finds rows already claimed (status != pending) and skips them.
Variant deleted before handler runs — shopify_query returns productVariant=null; all pending signups are marked failed with reason via try_catch catch arm.
Variant available field is false despite positive inventory — decision step inside try_catch returns early, preserving signups as pending for a genuine purchasable restock.
Email provider permanent bounce — email_send throws, try_catch catch arm sets status=failed with the rejection reason and logs the failed_permanent attempt.

sweep-product-signups.description: Sweep any product_signups rows stuck in a transitional state to prevent permanent stuck rows from blocking future notifications.

steps.purpose: sweep stale running rows in product_signups back to failed
record sweep results for ops observability

postconditions: no product_signups row remains stuck in a transitional state longer than the workflow TTL
edgeCases: No stale rows exist at sweep time — workflow.sweepStale returns empty array; log records swept_count=0.

platformGaps.gap: No batch email mutation exists for multiple recipients in a single Shopify or platform call, so per-signup email delivery inside the for_each loop requires one platform.email.send call per customer.
platformGaps.mitigation: Each signup iteration calls platform.email.send individually inside a try_catch; continueOnError=true on the for_each ensures a single send failure does not abort the remaining recipients.
platformGaps.uxImplication: Partial-success outcomes (some customers notified, some failed) are possible; the admin dashboard must display per-signup status so the merchant can identify and manually address failed deliveries.

platformGaps.gap: The inventory_levels/update webhook fires for every inventory adjustment (including decrements and transfers), not exclusively for zero-to-positive transitions.
platformGaps.mitigation: The recipe checks payload.available > 0 in a decision step and exits early when the quantity is not positive, ensuring decrements and same-level adjustments are treated as no-ops.

platformGaps.gap: Shopify does not provide a storefront customer access token in webhook payloads, so the widget GET route cannot rely on a Shopify-issued identity token; it falls back to a caller-supplied customer_email query parameter.
platformGaps.mitigation: The widget GET and POST routes accept customer_email directly in the request; the app trusts the value as supplied by the widget which reads it from the logged-in customer context via host.context.
platformGaps.uxImplication: Widget must pre-fill customer_email from the logged-in customer context before making API calls; for guests the email field must be shown as a manual input.

emailSpec.purpose: Notify a customer that a product variant they signed up for is back in stock and prompt them to purchase before it sells out again.

starterContent.subject: {{productTitle}} is back in stock!
starterContent.body:
Great news! {{productTitle}} — {{variantTitle}} is back in stock and available to purchase now.

Shop now before it sells out →

You're receiving this email because you signed up for a back-in-stock alert. You will not receive further notifications for this item.

uxExpectations.storefront: Widget should appear on sold-out product pages as a compact inline form — one email input field and a single 'Notify me' button. For logged-in customers, pre-fill the email field from host.context and allow one-click submission. Once signed up, replace the form with a confirmation message and an 'Unsubscribe' link. After the variant is restocked, the widget should revert to the standard add-to-cart UI.
uxExpectations.admin: Dashboard should lead with a status-tab navigation (All / Pending / Notified / Failed / Unsubscribed) so the merchant can immediately scan delivery health. Each row should show the customer email, product variant, signup date, and resolution date. Failed rows should surface the failure_reason inline so the merchant can act without drilling into a detail view. A summary count at the top of each tab gives at-a-glance volume.

edgeCases: A restock webhook fires while a previous delivery wave for the same variant is still in progress — the sql_claim atomic UPDATE WHERE status='pending' ensures each signup is claimed by exactly one wave; the second concurrent webhook finds no unclaimed rows and exits cleanly.

A customer holds a terminal signup row (notified, failed, or unsubscribed) and attempts to sign up again for the same variant — the ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING insert returns zero rows and the response returns success=true; the merchant should consider a UI flow to allow re-subscription after deletion of the terminal row if desired.

The notification_attempts table accumulates a failed_permanent row while the product_signups row is simultaneously updated to failed — both writes happen inside the same try_catch catch arm per iteration, but they are not wrapped in a sql_transaction; a crash between the two writes would leave the signup row in notified state with no attempt log, which the sweep cron would later correct.

product_signups.failure_reason is stored inline on the signup row and also in notification_attempts.failure_reason — these two values are written from the same emailError.message source in the same catch arm, so they will always agree; the denormalisation is intentional for fast admin display without a JOIN.

A customer uses two different email addresses to sign up for the same variant — each address creates a distinct signup row (the unique constraint is on customer_email + variant_external_id), and both receive independent notification emails on restock.

The SHOP_DOMAIN environment variable used to construct the product URL is missing at runtime — the compute step would produce a malformed URL; this must be validated at app startup and surfaced as a configuration error rather than silently emitting broken links in notification emails.
